one_line: Abyssinian-born statesman of Ahmadnagar, overseeing Deccan land revenue reforms and crop assessments.

appearance.age_look: late 40s, lean but sturdy build, upright posture of a seasoned commander-administrator
appearance.face: oval face with high cheekbones, medium-deep brown complexion, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, sharp observant eyes with calm stern gaze, default expression focused and assessing as if weighing reports
appearance.hair: short, tightly curled black hair mostly covered by a deep indigo Deccan-style turban wrapped low and firm, with a narrow white cloth band at the base and a small folded tail at the back
appearance.costume: long-sleeved white cotton jama (front-wrapping robe) reaching below the knees with a slightly flared skirt, worn over fitted churidar-style trousers in muted sand-beige; a sleeveless quilted cotton waistcoat in dark bottle-green over the jama, lightly padded to suggest travel and field work; wide woven cloth kamarband belt in maroon and gold wrapped twice at the waist with one neat knot, from which a small leather pouch hangs; simple dark brown leather mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes; minimal jewellery—one plain silver ring on the right hand and small silver stud earrings—evoking status but restraint; overall garments clean and practical, with very subtle block-printed border on the jama cuffs and hem in pale blue geometric motifs.
appearance.signature: A long rolled revenue survey scroll held in his left hand, sealed at one end with a red wax-like stamp and tied with a thin golden cord, while a plain wooden writing board with a tied reed pen and ink-pot case is tucked under his right arm.

ref_desc: Malik Ambar is a lean, late-40s man with medium-brown skin, short-curled hair under a deep indigo turban, white jama, sand-beige trousers, dark green waistcoat, maroon-gold belt, brown mojari shoes, and he carries a sealed revenue scroll with a small writing board.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Malik Ambar as a dignified Deccan revenue chief: a lean, late-40s man with medium-brown complexion, oval face, short black curls mostly covered by a deep indigo turban wrapped low and firm with a narrow white band. Give him sharp, observant eyes and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, his default expression focused and serious as if evaluating land reports. Dress him in a long-sleeved white cotton jama that wraps in front and falls below the knees, with a subtly pale-blue block-printed geometric border at the cuffs and hem, worn over fitted sand-beige churidar trousers. Add a sleeveless quilted cotton waistcoat in dark bottle-green over the jama, lightly padded and practical, and a wide maroon kamarband belt with thin gold stripes wrapped twice at the waist, knotted neatly, with a small leather pouch hanging from it. Put simple dark brown mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes on his feet and very minimal jewellery—a plain silver ring and tiny silver stud earrings—to suggest status without flamboyance. In his left hand, show a long rolled revenue survey scroll tied with a thin golden cord and sealed with a red stamp, and under his right arm tuck a plain wooden writing board with a tied reed pen and small ink-pot case. Use a palette dominated by white, indigo, bottle green, maroon, and sand-beige, and pose him upright and composed, as if standing in a Deccan village field ready to supervise crop assessment.
